newsitem.title: CHINA: Bank of China pledges fair play in post-97 HK.
newsitem.headline: Bank of China pledges fair play in post-97 HK.

text.p: The state-owned commercial Bank of China will observe the principle of fair play in competition with Hong Kong counterparts after the return of the British colony to Beijing rule in 1997, state media said on Sunday.
The bank will work with Hong Kong banks to ensure stable and prosperous financial trade in the territory, the China Daily Business Weekly quoted Bank of China (BOC) President Wang Xuebing as saying.
"The bright prospect also paves the way for broader contacts between BOC and the financial institutions in the region," Wang said.

The BOC began business contacts with Hong Kong financial bodies in the 1950s and now has agents in 19 local financial institutions and 78 branches of its foreign financial units in Hong Kong, Wang said.
From 1995 to the first half of this year, the BOC and its correspondent banks in Hong Kong made some 80,000 settlement deals with total value exceeding $10 billion, Wang said.
In the past two years, BOC achieved total trade financing in Hong Kong of $700 million, the newspaper said.
